## Modular Synth Performance Prep

Hey_nice_marmot_ is gearing up for their first live modular synthesizer performance this November, and the social media inbox is buzzing with advice for the upcoming set. The artist has opted to strip down their setup significantly to simplify travel and studio reconfiguration, leaving traditional keyboard synths behind. Instead, the rig relies on an Ableton Push 3 to launch MIDI and audio clips, while the sonic texture is driven by DFAM and Mother 32 modules. Vocals and bass processing are handled by Maths and Data Bender units.

In a shared 23-minute practice video, the performer outlines three primary challenges: navigating the Push’s session view without getting lost, maintaining the discipline to reset the modular patch to a safe starting state between songs, and troubleshooting unpredictable issues during recording. The community response has been supportive, with experienced performers offering tips on avoiding common beginner mistakes in similar hybrid setups.

## Sonic Spin-Offs and Vintage Comics

Nostalgia for the Game Gear era is alive and well on Bluesky and Tumblr, where fans are debating the relative fun factor of two Tails exclusives: *Tails Adventure* and *Tails Skypatrol*. The discussion asks which title stands up better in retrospect, contrasting *Skypatrol*’s side-scrolling action with *Adventure*’s open-world exploration. It’s a tight cluster of conversation focusing on these specific handheld spin-offs.

In a related vintage discovery, @Sonic The Hedgeblog shared a piece of comic art from Archie Comics’ *Sonic the Hedgehog* issue #38. The post highlights "Bat Sonic," a parody cover from the "Bedtime Tails!" arc. The artwork is noted for its distinct parody style compared to the main series, serving as a niche collectible detail for dedicated fans. The posts were identical across platforms, emphasizing the visual significance of this specific issue.

## AI Protection and Toy Hall of Fame

A skeptical tone emerged regarding data poisoning tools like Nightshade and Glaze, which are designed to protect images from unauthorized AI training. A user on Bluesky asked for recommendations, only to receive a blunt reply from @Doll: "they don't work though." This comment reflects a growing consensus in this cluster that there is a gap between the availability of these protection methods and their actual performance in real-world scenarios.

Meanwhile, the finalists for the 2026 National Toy Hall of Fame have been announced in Rochester, NY. The lineup is diverse, featuring Care Bears, BINGO, Monster High, and Pokemon Cards. The nominee list also includes Sorry!, Mouse Trap, Slide, Bop It!, Mahjong, Yahtzee, and Tickle Me Elmo. One commenter shared a lighthearted hope that Sorry! makes the cut, anticipating the charm of the local Western New York accent pronouncing the title as “SARREE!”

## Quick Hits

*   **QUEST 64 Confusion:** Users on Bluesky discussed the upcoming title *QUEST 64*, with many surprised to learn it is a native game rather than a homebrew or PC title with an N64 aesthetic. The official account clarified this common misconception.
*   **B&W Photography Economics:** In 4chan’s /fgt/ (Film General) thread, users debated the best developer kit for black-and-white photography. Rodinal was praised over Ilford Fine-Grain for its multi-year shelf life and cost-effectiveness; 1L of Rodinal can process hundreds of rolls compared to Ilford’s limited capacity and short post-opening lifespan.
*   **Beginner Darkroom Advice:** A user sought the easiest chemicals for home B&W development, weighing pre-composed Ilford and Jobo kits against harder-to-handle options. The discussion centered on accessibility for newcomers.
*   **Ilford Kit Missing Bag:** A practical complaint arose regarding Ilford developing kits, with a user noting they do not include a changing bag, a necessary addition for setup.
*   **Gear vs. Skill:** On 4chan’s /gear/ board, users debated the new motto: "gear only matters if your photo doesn't suck." The conversation highlighted the tension between consumerist urges to upgrade equipment and the realization that skill is the primary driver of image quality.
*   **Old Hardware Skepticism:** A user praised the aesthetic of "old hardware photography," but another countered with experience from a Game Boy Color, citing "fucking trash and unusable" photos. This highlighted the divide between nostalgic ambiance and functional low-resolution reality.
*   **Botanical Banter:** In the /rpt/ thread, a botanical photo with glossy green foliage and strong backlighting drew comments on texture and contrast. One user humorously criticized the composition for cropping the subject's "ass," suggesting the framing was imperfect.

Any beginner mistakes to avoid? — I've got my first gig booked in November, so I've been practicing ideas for how to get the studio on the road and performing live.   I've decided to focus on the modular only for live shows, launching MIDI and audio clips with the Ableton Push 3, leaving the keyboard synths at home. The thought of lugging multiple keys around for unpaid gigs 2 hours away—then having to rewire my studio again afterwards—doesn't spark joy.   If you've performed live with a similar setup, do you have any tips for me? What are the common beginner mistakes you see people making?   Things I've noticed already:     Feels easy to get lost on the Push's session view.   Getting the the full modular back into a starting state requires discipline I apparently lack   Every time I press record, some new issue I've never experienced before pops up and I have to troubleshoot, which'll be a fuck up on the night.     In this vid I'm launching a bunch of things off the Push and performing on the DFAM & Mother 32 live, with Maths and Data Bender chopping the vocals and bass lines up.   https://youtu.be/tZm0sRHRpHk?si=47bZWlPWF9I9lhRg Posted by u/Hey_nice_marmot_ · [comments]

representative_texts: @4529692 - /p/ — /fgt/ - Film General Thread — >>4529683 I would also be interested in an experienced answer as I'm putting together a B&W dev kit. From my research, you pick between rodinal and fine-grain, which are just as easy to use. The main difference is that fine-grain has a much shorter shelf life once opened and even worse if half empty, from 6 to 2 months. It's also more expensive per roll, 1L can develop only 10 rolls. In comparison Rodinal has years of shelf life and 1L will last hundreds of rolls. Appart from that the other baths and equipment is the same. I dont know the jobo kit but in the store I go they have an illford kit and it's absurdly expensive for no reason. Look into what you'd save if you bought stuff separately.
